html:
This 2012 video visits an anechoic chamber in Minnesota, at Orfield Laboratories in Minneapolis, billed as the quietest room in the world, with background noise that reaches negative decibels. Anechoic chambers in general use sound-absorbing wedges to suppress reflections, which lets them keep sound pressure in the room extremely low for acoustic experiments.

Fanyu Meng then poses a question. The anechoic chamber that Aalto University in Finland has rebuilt over the past two years is said to reach −2 dB and is billed as the quietest room in Finland (see the account’s earlier article on acoustics labs in Europe). So which of the two chambers wins?

He also added bilingual subtitles, produced with a website that translates subtitles into Chinese automatically. They are far from perfect, he admits, so the English is the reference, though that is not entirely accurate either. ;)

Shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
